name: Burial
system_prompt:
You will be given one or more molecular structures and a question about them.
Answer using only the information supplied in the prompt. Do not use tools or
external resources.

Protein residues are identified as <chain>:<one-letter amino-acid code><author
residue number>. For example, A:V22 is valine 22 in chain A. When asked for a
residue, use exactly this format. When asked for a list, return a comma-separated
list. Do not include additional residues.

Place the machine-readable answer after FINAL: using the format requested by
the question. You may reason before the final answer, but only the FINAL field
will be scored.
question:
Question: Is residue A:R204 buried or solvent-exposed? Use the solvent-accessible surface area of the residue relative to its maximum accessible area: buried means at most 0.20, solvent-exposed means at least 0.40. Answer buried or solvent-exposed.

Answer with exactly one of the listed categories.
Example: FINAL: helix

qwen.text:
Based on the provided coordinates, residue A:R204 is the C-terminal residue of the chain. Its side chain atoms extend into empty space with no other protein residues or groups within close proximity (< 5 Å). C-terminal residues with unobstructed side chains typically have a high relative solvent-accessible surface area (well above 0.40). Therefore, it is solvent-exposed.

FINAL: solvent-exposed
